title: Effectivity and full faithfulness of fpqc descent for quasi-coherent sheaves
author: The Stacks Project Authors
source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: For an fpqc covering of a scheme, the proposition asserts that every descent datum on quasi-coherent sheaves is effective and that the comparison functor from quasi-coherent modules to descent data is fully faithful (statement lines 1800-1810). The proof is a three-part argument. It begins by reducing to coverings that are standard affine over the members of an affine open covering of the base, exhibiting for each member a standard affine covering refining the given one (proof lines 1812-1835). Faithfulness is then a stalkwise argument using faithful flatness of the local ring maps induced by the covering morphisms (proof lines 1842-1851). Fullness and essential surjectivity are handled together: a morphism of descent data pulls back to the standard coverings and glues over the affine pieces, the agreement on overlaps being checked through a common refinement and the faithfulness just proved (proof lines 1853-1880), while a descent datum pulls back to the standard coverings, is realized there, and the resulting local modules are glued after checking the cocycle condition again by faithfulness (proof lines 1882-1904). The author closes by stating that the verification that the canonical descent datum of the glued module is isomorphic to the one started with is omitted (proof lines 1905-1907). The claim is H3: three genuinely different arguments, with the gluing and the refinement bookkeeping being original work.
